headline: BRTC launches 'Pink Bus' service for women in Dhaka
summary: The new fleet features all-female crews, including drivers and conductors, to ensure safer and more comfortable commutes for women.
details: The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) has officially launched a special 'Pink Bus' service in Dhaka to ensure safe and comfortable travel for women.
The service was inaugurated on Tuesday (August 18) at the BRTC Dhaka Truck Depot in Tejgaon.
Initially, 10 buses will operate on key routes, including New Market to Motijheel, Taltala to Motijheel, Demra to GPO, and Mirpur-10 and 12 to Motijheel.
Other routes include Mohammadpur to Motijheel and Abdullahpur to Motijheel, as well as a service from Gazipur to the Airport.
A unique feature of these buses is that the passengers, drivers, and conductors are all women.
Beyond Dhaka, the BRTC is also introducing this special service in Bogura and Chattogram.
The BRTC hopes that this initiative will not only increase safety and comfort for female passengers but also create more employment opportunities for women in the transport sector.
caption:
All-female crews, all-female passengers. BRTC's new 'Pink Buses' are hitting the roads of Dhaka!

The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) has officially launched a special 'Pink Bus' service in Dhaka to ensure safe and comfortable travel for women.

The service was inaugurated on Tuesday (August 18) at the BRTC Dhaka Truck Depot in Tejgaon.

Initially, 10 buses will operate on key routes, including New Market to Motijheel, Taltala to Motijheel, Demra to GPO, and Mirpur-10 and 12 to Motijheel.

Other routes include Mohammadpur to Motijheel and Abdullahpur to Motijheel, as well as a service from Gazipur to the Airport.

A unique feature of these buses is that the passengers, drivers, and conductors are all women.

Beyond Dhaka, the BRTC is also introducing this special service in Bogura and Chattogram.

The BRTC hopes that this initiative will not only increase safety and comfort for female passengers but also create more employment opportunities for women in the transport sector.

headline: Australia axed opener Weatherald after Bangladesh rout
summary: Matthew Renshaw returns to the Test squad after three years as Australia reshuffles their top order following a disappointing first Test against Bangladesh.
details: Australia has made a significant change to their squad for the second and final ICC World Test Championship fixture against Bangladesh in Mackay.
Opener Jake Weatherald has been dropped from the 13-player squad after contributing scores of just 23 and 0 in the first Test, where Australia was bundled out for 198 in the first innings.
Left-hander Matthew Renshaw has been recalled to the Test arena for the first time in over three years, replacing Weatherald.
Renshaw's last Test appearance was in Delhi against India in 2023, as a concussion substitute for David Warner.
Despite a lack of runs, regular No. 3 Marnus Labuschagne retains his place, though coach Andrew McDonald admitted the batter has some work to do.
Back-up keeper-batter Josh Inglis and reserve bowler Scott Boland remain in the squad for the second Test, which begins this Saturday.

The full squad includes Pat Cummins, Scott Boland, the Carey, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Marnus Labuschagne, Matthew Renshaw, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc, and Beau Webster.
caption:
Australia drops an opener after a shocking rout by Bangladesh! 🏏

Australia has made a significant change to their squad for the second and final ICC World Test Championship fixture against Bangladesh in Mackay.

Opener Jake Weatherald has been dropped from the 13-player squad after contributing scores of just 23 and 0 in the first Test, where Australia was bundled out for 198 in the first innings.

Left-hander Matthew Renshaw has been recalled to the Test arena for the first time in over three years, replacing Weatherald.

Renshaw's last Test appearance was in Delhi against India in 2023, as a concussion substitute for David Warner.

Despite a lack of runs, regular No. 3 Marnus Labuschagne retains his place, though coach Andrew McDonald admitted the batter has some work to do.

Back-up keeper-batter Josh Inglis and reserve bowler Scott Boland remain in the squad for the second Test, which begins this Saturday.

The full squad includes Pat Cummins, Scott Boland, the Carey, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Marnus Labuschagne, Matthew Renshaw, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc, and Beau Webster.
